title: Prevent compressed requests from exhausting the server
scope: Remove GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828 from Express's installed and locked body-parser resolution using a compatible patched dependency. Preserve JSON, URL-encoded, multipart, body limits, authentication and safe errors. No unrelated dependency updates, audit waivers, production data changes or deployment.
why: The security audit and browser compatibility checks are required alongside compiler and HTTP regression tests.
coverage: docs/validation/manifest.json test-heavy: 900000 ms; security-audit, typecheck, unit-tests including dependency-network-security.test.ts and routes.test.ts, browser-tests through scripts/run-browser-tests.mjs. Invoke gate:run with generated task context.

approval.direction: Repair the compressed request body-parser advisory and implement the specified guards
approval.applicability: Compatible dependency repair and regression coverage only

assertions.check: Every installed and locked Express consumer resolves body-parser >=2.4.0 in major 2; portable locked installation retains the resolution.
A finite heap- and time-bounded child receives compressed frames with delayed trailing bytes, survives, handles a subsequent valid request and exits normally.

Real HTTP tests preserve JSON and URL-encoded parsing, reject malformed and oversized bodies, and leave multipart for its own parser. Existing route and browser tests cover authentication and uploads.

regression.rationale: Security and availability repair at the existing Express parsing boundary.
regression.covers: R1 vulnerable body-parser resolution; R2 compressed trailing-byte process crash; R3 parsing compatibility
regression.assertion: Assert patched consumer and lockfile versions, bounded successful child exit after delayed compressed trailers and a subsequent request, valid parsing, safe malformed/limit rejection and multipart bypass.
